question: A 36-year-old woman comes to the physician because of painless lesions on the vulva that she first noticed 2 days ago. She does not have any urinary symptoms. She has gastroesophageal reflux disease for which she takes omeprazole. She has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 10 years. She is sexually active with multiple partners and uses condoms inconsistently. Examination shows clusters of several 3- to 5-mm raised lesions with a rough texture on the vulva. Application of a dilute acetic acid solution turns the lesions white. An HIV test is negative. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Painless lesions on vulva" -> "Clusters of 3- to 5-mm raised lesions" -> "Rough texture of lesions" -> "Application of dilute acetic acid turns lesions white" -> "Suggestive of genital warts (condylomata acuminata)" -> "Management typically involves cryotherapy" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Painless lesions on vulva" -> "Negative HIV test" -> "Sexually active with multiple partners" -> "Inconsistent condom use" -> "High risk for sexually transmitted infections" -> "Lesions consistent with HPV infection" -> "Cryotherapy is a common treatment option" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Painless lesions on vulva" -> "Lesions turn white with acetic acid" -> "Indicates possible HPV infection" -> "No signs of bacterial or viral infection" -> "Cryotherapy is effective for HPV-related lesions" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Painless lesions on vulva" -> "Rough textured lesions" -> "Negative HIV test" -> "High-risk sexual behavior" -> "Lesions likely due to HPV" -> "Cryotherapy is a standard treatment" -> 75%
analysis: The patient's presentation is consistent with genital warts (condylomata acuminata), which are caused by human papillomavirus (HPV). The lesions are painless, raised, and turn white with acetic acid application, which is characteristic of HPV lesions. The most appropriate next step in management for external genital warts is cryotherapy, which is a common treatment option. Other options listed, such as benzathine penicillin, topical mometasone, radiotherapy, and oral acyclovir, are not indicated for the treatment of HPV-related lesions.
